# DataFrames: Polars Only

Applies to all library code under `pkgs/`.

## Rule

**Polars is the only DataFrame type in the library's interfaces.** Any function, method or class that accepts
or returns tabular data uses `polars.DataFrame` (or `polars.LazyFrame`, see below). pandas is not supported as
an input or return type.

- **One type per parameter and return.** No `pd.DataFrame | pl.DataFrame` unions, no `to_pandas: bool` flags,
  no "accepts either and converts" helpers, no parallel `_pd` variants of functions.
- **Converting is the caller's job.** Anyone who wants pandas converts at their own boundary:
  `df.to_pandas()` / `pl.from_pandas(pdf)`.
- **No pandas dependency in library code.** Don't import pandas in `pkgs/`. If a third-party API only speaks
  pandas, convert right at that call site and hand polars back to the rest of the library.
- **Polars-native operations:** expressions, `DataFrame.sql` / `pl.SQLContext` (eg `ds.data.db.SmashDb`), and
  parquet for storage (see `.agents/instructions/pkgs.md`, "`ds/data` Conventions").

## Why

- **One way to do things.** Supporting several input/return types for the same function tends to grow into
  every function supporting both, with conversions, dtype mismatches and a doubled test surface. Refusing it
  at the first function keeps the library small and predictable.
- **Polars already runs the library.** SmashDb, the parquet tables and SQL queries are all polars. Mixing in
  pandas would add conversions with no benefit.

## Eager vs lazy

- **Public functions return `pl.DataFrame` (eager)** unless laziness is the point of the API. Callers
  shouldn't have to remember `.collect()`.
- **Use `pl.LazyFrame` / `scan_*` internally** for large inputs or pushdown. `SmashDb` scans parquet lazily
  and returns eager results from `sql()`.
- **A function that is deliberately lazy** (eg builds a query plan for the caller to extend) returns
  `pl.LazyFrame` and says so in its name or docstring.

## Boundaries

- **pydantic-ai tools:** a DataFrame can't be serialized to the model, so tools return
  `ds.ai.table.TableResult.from_df(df)`. Python callers rebuild the frame with `.to_df()`. See
  `.agents/instructions/pkgs.md`, "pydantic-ai Conventions".
- **Scripts, notebooks and `local/` experiments** may use whatever they like, pandas included. This spec
  only covers library interfaces in `pkgs/`.
